intro: How many kids are on the bus? How many pennies are in the jar? Every day we need to know how many. Counting is how we find out. In this unit you will learn to count the right way. One number for each thing. The last number tells how many.
Big numbers are hard to count by ones. So we make groups of ten. Ten pennies go in a bag. Ten straws go in a bundle. Then we count the bags. A number like 64 tells us six tens and four ones.

By the end you will count to 100. You will count by twos, fives and tens. You will tell which group has more. You will read and write numbers with tens and ones. And you will compare them with >, < and =.
bigQuestion: How do numbers tell us how many, and why do we group things in tens?

test.q: Dan counts 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. How many things does he have?
test.why: The last number he said was 9. So there are 9 things.

test.q: Count by tens: 70, 80, 90, what comes next?
test.why: Each jump adds ten. 90 and 10 more is 100.
Zero means none. We write it 0.

test.q: Start at 15. Count on 2 more. What number do you say last?
test.why: Start at 15, then say 16, 17. The last number is 17.

test.q: Which has fewer: 6 cats or 8 dogs?
test.why: 6 is smaller than 8. The cats are the smaller group.

test.q: What number is 5 tens and 3 ones?
test.why: 5 tens is 50. 50 and 3 is 53. Tens go first.

test.q: 16 is one ten and how many ones?
test.why: 16 is ten and 6 more. So it has 6 ones.
2 tens is less than 9 tens. So 29 < 92.
5 tens become 4 tens. The ones stay 0. So it is 40.

test.q: Count by fives: 20, 25, 30, what comes next?
test.why: Each jump adds five. 30 and 5 more is 35.

write.prompt: Show the number 36 with rods and cubes. Then show 36 a second way. Explain how you know both ways show the same number.
tips: Draw your blocks and count them out loud.
Tell what the 3 means and what the 6 means.
Check by counting by tens, then counting on by ones.

title: Counting and Numbers

chapters.title: Counting and Comparing
chapters.bigQuestion: How do we know for sure how many things are in a group?

story.title: The Bus Count
story.kicker: The class is going to the zoo, but first Mr. Ortiz has to know how many kids are on the bus.
paragraphs: The bus is here. The whole class is going to Lincoln Park Zoo in Chicago. Mr. Ortiz stands by the door. He needs to know how many kids get on. If he loses count, someone might get left behind.
He touches each head as a kid climbs on. One. Two. Three. He goes slow. He says one number for each kid. Nobody gets skipped. Nobody gets counted twice.
The last kid gets on. Mr. Ortiz says twenty-two. So there are 22 kids on the bus. He writes 22 on his clipboard. He does not need to count again.
At the zoo, the kids move all around. But the number stays the same. When it is time to go home, Mr. Ortiz counts again. He needs to hear twenty-two.
story.think: Why did Mr. Ortiz touch each head as he counted? What could go wrong if he counted fast?

lessons.title: One Number for Each Thing
lessons.mainIdea: Say one number for each thing you count. Do not skip any. Do not count one twice.
reading: Mia has some apples on the table. She touches one apple and says one. She touches the next and says two. Then three. Each apple gets one number. This is *one-to-one* counting.
Sometimes we count too fast. We say five but only touch four apples. Slow down. Touch each thing. Move it to the side after you count it. Then you will not count it twice.

words.d: one number for each thing you count, with no skips and no repeats

look.title: Buttons in a Row
look.text: Look at a row of buttons. There are six buttons. Ben touches the first button and says one. He touches the second and says two. He skips the third button. He says three on the fourth button. What happened?
look.prompt: Count the buttons again the slow way. Touch each one. What number do you say last?

check.q: You count five toy cars. What should you do with each car?
choices: Skip it if it is small
check.why: Each thing gets one number. Five cars get the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

check.q: Sam has 4 blocks. He counts 1, 2, 3, 3. What did he do wrong?
choices: He said the same number for two blocks
check.why: He said 3 twice. Four blocks should get 1, 2, 3, 4.

check.q: Ana counts 3 pencils. Which count is right?
check.why: The numbers go in order: 1, 2, 3. The last number is 3, so there are 3 pencils.

lessons.title: The Last Number Tells How Many
lessons.mainIdea: The last number you say tells how many things there are in all.
reading: Leo counts his crayons. He says one, two, three, four, five. He stops at five. So Leo has five crayons. The last number tells *how many*.
Now Leo moves the crayons around. He puts them in a circle. Does he have to count again? No. It is still five. Moving things does not change how many.
Try it. Count seven coins in a row. Now spread them out. Count again. Still seven. The number does not change.

words.d: the total number of things in a group

look.title: Toys in the Bin
look.cite: an example count from a classroom toy bin
look.prompt: Which toy has the most in the bin? How many balls are there?

check.q: Kim counts 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. How many things does she have?
check.why: The last number she said was 6. So she has 6 things.

check.q: Ray counts 8 rocks in a row. He moves them into a pile. How many rocks now?
choices: Ray must count again to know
check.why: Moving things does not change how many. There are still 8 rocks.

check.q: In the toy bin table, how many balls are there?
check.why: The balls row says 3. Cars are 4 and dolls are 2.

lessons.title: Zero Means None
lessons.mainIdea: Zero means there is nothing to count. We write it as 0.
reading: Jo has a plate. There are three cookies on it. She eats one. Now there are two. She eats one more. Now there is one. She eats the last cookie. Now there are none. We say *zero*. We write 0.
Zero is a number. It comes before one. Count down: 3, 2, 1, 0. An empty box has zero toys. An empty hand has zero coins.

words.d: the number for none; we write it as 0

look.title: The Empty Cup
look.text: Look at two cups. The first cup has four marbles. The second cup has no marbles at all. Point to the cup with zero marbles. Now take one marble out of the first cup. How many are left there?
look.prompt: How many marbles are in the empty cup? Say the number and write it.

check.q: A box has no crayons in it. How many crayons is that?
check.why: None means zero. We write 0.

check.q: Count down: 3, 2, 1, what comes next?
check.why: Counting down, the number after 1 is 0. Zero comes before one.

check.q: Which one shows zero?
check.why: An empty plate has no cookies. No cookies is zero cookies.

lessons.title: Counting On
lessons.mainIdea: You can start counting from any number. You do not have to start at one.
reading: Max has 5 stickers in a pile. He knows there are 5. He gets 3 more. He does not start at one. He says five, then six, seven, eight. Now he has 8 stickers. This is counting on.
Start at the number you know. Say the next numbers. Start at 12: 13, 14, 15. Start at 27: 28, 29, 30. Counting on saves time.

words.d: start at a number you know and keep counting up from there

look.title: Stickers on a Page
look.text: Look at a page of stickers. The first row has 10 stickers. You know that. The second row has 4 more. Put your finger on the last sticker in the first row. Say ten. Now count on: eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen.
look.prompt: Start at 10 and count on 4 more. What number do you land on?

check.q: Start at 6. Count on 2 more. What number do you say last?
check.why: Start at 6, then say 7, 8. The last number is 8.

check.q: What number comes right after 19?
check.why: Counting up from 19, the next number is 20.

check.q: Ava has 14 beads. She adds 3 more. She counts on: 15, 16, 17. How many beads?
check.why: Start at 14 and count on 3: 15, 16, 17. She has 17 beads.

lessons.title: Counting by Tens
lessons.mainIdea: Count by tens: 10, 20, 30, up to 100. Each jump adds ten.
reading: A dime is worth ten cents. Ten pennies make one dime. Count dimes by tens: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. Five dimes are 50 cents. Say it fast. Ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty.
Keep going up. 60, 70, 80, 90, 100. Ten tens make one hundred. Counting by tens is a *skip count*. You skip the numbers in between.
Hear the pattern. Each word ends the same way. Twenty, thirty, forty. Each one is ten more than the last.

words.d: count by jumps, like 10, 20, 30, instead of by ones
the number 100; ten groups of ten

look.title: Dimes and Cents
look.cite: U.S. coin values: one dime is 10 cents
look.prompt: How many cents would 5 dimes be? What comes next in the table?

check.q: Count by tens: 10, 20, 30, what comes next?
check.why: Each jump adds ten. 30 and 10 more is 40.

check.q: How many cents are 3 dimes?
check.why: Each dime is 10 cents. Count 10, 20, 30. That is 30 cents.

check.q: What number is ten more than 70?
check.why: Counting by tens, 70 then 80. Ten more than 70 is 80.

lessons.title: Counting by Twos and Fives
lessons.mainIdea: Count by twos: 2, 4, 6, 8. Count by fives: 5, 10, 15, 20.
reading: Socks come in pairs. A *pair* is two socks. Count socks by twos. 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Five pairs are 10 socks. Each jump adds two.
Your hand has five fingers. Count fingers by fives. 5, 10, 15, 20. Four hands are 20 fingers. A nickel is worth five cents. Count nickels by fives too.

words.d: two things that go together, like two socks

look.title: Hands in the Air
look.text: Look at three friends. Each friend holds up one hand. Each hand has five fingers. Count by fives. Five, ten, fifteen. Now a fourth friend holds up a hand. Count on by five one more time.
look.prompt: How many fingers are up when four hands are raised? Count by fives to check.

check.q: Count by twos: 2, 4, 6, what comes next?
check.why: Each jump adds two. 6 and 2 more is 8.

check.q: Count by fives: 5, 10, 15, what comes next?
check.why: Each jump adds five. 15 and 5 more is 20.

check.q: How many socks are in 3 pairs?
check.why: Count by twos: 2, 4, 6. Three pairs are 6 socks.

lessons.title: More, Fewer, the Same
lessons.mainIdea: Match things up one to one to see which group has more, fewer, or the same.
reading: Tia has 4 red cubes. Ben has 6 blue cubes. Line them up. Put one red next to one blue. Two blue cubes have no partner. So Ben has *more*. Tia has *fewer*.
Now count instead. 6 is bigger than 4. So 6 cubes is more than 4 cubes. If both had 4, the groups would be the *same*. Matching and counting both work.

words.d: a bigger amount than another group
a smaller amount than another group
the two groups have an equal number

look.title: Fruit on the Snack Table
look.prompt: Which two fruits have the same number? Which fruit has the fewest?

check.q: Lee has 7 cars. Kay has 9 cars. Who has more?
check.why: 9 is bigger than 7. Kay has more cars.

check.q: Which group has fewer: 3 dogs or 5 cats?
check.why: 3 is smaller than 5. The dogs are the smaller group.

check.q: In the fruit table, which fruit has the fewest?
check.why: Bananas are 3. Apples and oranges are 5. Three is the smallest.

lessons.title: Writing Numbers and Number Words
lessons.mainIdea: Every number has a numeral and a word. 7 is seven. 12 is twelve.
reading: We write numbers two ways. We write the *numeral* 5. We write the *number word* five. Both mean the same amount. Count 5 fingers. Write 5. Write five.
Here are the words from 0 to 10. Zero, one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. Then come the teens. Eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen.
Some numbers are tricky to write. A 6 and a 9 look alike upside down. Watch the direction. Practice writing 0 to 20 on a line.

words.d: a written number sign, like 5 or 12
a number written in letters, like five or twelve

look.title: Numbers on the Lockers
look.text: Look at a row of lockers. Each one has a numeral. The first says 11. The next says 12. Then 13, 14, 15. One locker tag fell off. It goes between 15 and 17. Say the number words as you walk down the row.
look.prompt: What numeral is on the missing tag? Write it and say its word.

check.q: Which numeral matches the word eight?
check.why: Eight is written 8. Eighteen is 18.

check.q: What is the number word for 12?
check.why: 12 is twelve. 2 is two and 20 is twenty.

check.q: What number is missing? 15, 16, __, 18
check.why: Counting up: 15, 16, 17, 18. The missing number is 17.

review.q: Jen counts 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. How many things does she have?
review.why: The last number she said was 7. So there are 7 things.

review.q: Count by tens: 40, 50, 60, what comes next?
review.why: Each jump adds ten. 60 and 10 more is 70.

review.q: A bag has no marbles. What number tells how many?
Start at 8. Count on 3 more. What number do you say last?
review.why: Start at 8, then say 9, 10, 11. The last number is 11.

review.q: Which has more: 5 apples or 3 pears?
review.why: 5 is bigger than 3. The apples are the bigger group.

review.q: Count by fives: 10, 15, 20, what comes next?
review.why: Each jump adds five. 20 and 5 more is 25.

chapters.title: Tens and Ones
chapters.bigQuestion: Why do we group things in tens, and what does each digit in a number tell us?

story.title: The Penny Bags
story.kicker: The class store jar is full of pennies, and nobody wants to count them one by one.
paragraphs: The class store has a big jar of pennies. Kids pay with them. Now the jar is full. Ms. Bell asks, how many pennies do we have? Counting by ones would take all day.
Rosa has an idea. Count ten pennies. Put them in a small bag. Then count ten more. Make another bag. Soon the table has bags of ten. A few loose pennies are left over.

The class counts the bags by tens. Ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty. Then they count on the loose pennies. Sixty-one, sixty-two, sixty-three, sixty-four. There are 64 pennies. Six bags of ten and four ones.
Ms. Bell writes 64 on the board. The 6 stands for six bags. The 4 stands for four loose pennies. Two little numbers tell the whole story.
story.think: Why did the class bag the pennies in tens instead of counting all of them one by one?

lessons.title: A Bundle of Ten
lessons.mainIdea: Ten ones make one ten. We can count a bundle of ten as one group.
reading: Ali has ten straws. She counts them. 1, 2, 3, up to 10. She puts a rubber band around them. Now she has one *bundle*. One bundle is one *ten*. It is still ten straws.
Ten ones make one ten. That is the big idea. When we have ten small things, we can group them. Then we count groups. It is faster.

words.d: a group of things held together; a bundle of ten is one ten
a group of ten ones

look.title: Straws on the Desk
look.text: Look at a desk with straws. There is one bundle with a rubber band. It holds ten straws. Next to it are three loose straws. Say the bundle as ten. Then count on the loose straws. Eleven, twelve, thirteen.
look.prompt: How many straws are on the desk in all? How many bundles could you make from 20 straws?

check.q: How many ones make one ten?
check.why: A ten is a group of ten ones. Count 1 to 10 and bundle them.

check.q: Ali has 2 bundles of ten straws. How many straws?
check.why: Count the bundles by tens: 10, 20. Two tens are 20 straws.

check.q: You have 30 pennies. How many bags of ten can you make?
check.why: Count by tens: 10, 20, 30. That is 3 bags of ten.

lessons.title: Teen Numbers
lessons.mainIdea: A teen number is one ten and some more ones. 14 is ten and four.
reading: Ken has 14 grapes. He makes a group of ten. Four grapes are left over. So 14 is one ten and four ones. Say it: ten and four more.
Every *teen number* works this way. 11 is ten and one. 12 is ten and two. 15 is ten and five. 19 is ten and nine. The 1 in front means one ten.
Watch the words. Fourteen sounds like four and ten. Sixteen sounds like six and ten. Eleven and twelve are the odd ones. Just remember them.

words.d: a number from 11 to 19; one ten and some ones

look.title: Teen Numbers as Ten and More
look.cite: each teen number is one ten plus some ones
look.prompt: What would ten and 9 be? Which row shows 15?

check.q: 17 is one ten and how many ones?
check.why: 17 is ten and 7 more. So it has 7 ones.

check.q: What is ten and 3 more?
check.why: Start at ten and count on 3: 11, 12, 13. That is 13.

check.q: Which number is one ten and 8 ones?
check.why: One ten and 8 ones is 18. The 1 means one ten.

lessons.title: The Ten Frame
lessons.mainIdea: A ten frame has ten boxes. A full frame is one ten. Extra dots are the ones.
reading: A *ten frame* is a box with ten spaces. Two rows of five. Put one dot in each space. When it is full, you have ten. You do not need to count.
Rae shows 13 with frames. She fills one frame. That is ten. She puts 3 dots in a second frame. Ten and three is 13. One full frame and 3 more.
A ten frame also shows how far to ten. If 7 spaces are full, 3 are empty. So 7 needs 3 more to make ten.

words.d: a box with ten spaces in two rows of five, used to show numbers

look.title: Dots in the Frames
look.text: Look at two ten frames. The top frame is full. All ten spaces have a dot. The bottom frame has dots in six spaces. Four spaces are empty. Say the top frame as ten. Then count on the dots in the bottom frame.
look.prompt: What number do the two frames show? How many more dots would fill the bottom frame?

check.q: A ten frame has 8 dots. How many spaces are empty?
check.why: The frame has 10 spaces. 8 are full, so 2 are empty. 8 and 2 make 10.

check.q: One full frame and 5 more dots show what number?
check.why: A full frame is ten. Ten and 5 more is 15.

check.q: How many spaces are in one ten frame?
check.why: A ten frame has two rows of five. That is 10 spaces.

lessons.title: Two-Digit Numbers
lessons.mainIdea: In a two-digit number, the first digit counts tens. The second digit counts ones.
reading: The class has 64 pennies. Six bags of ten. Four loose ones. We write 64. The 6 is in the *tens place*. The 4 is in the *ones place*. Six tens and four ones.
Look at 37. The 3 means three tens. That is 30. The 7 means seven ones. 30 and 7 is 37. Now look at 73. Is that three tens? No. 73 is seven tens and three ones. Order matters.
A common mistake is to mix up the places. 25 is not the same as 52. Say the tens first. Two tens and five ones is 25. Each *digit* has its own job.

words.d: one of the number signs 0 to 9; the number 47 has two digits
the spot on the left in a two-digit number; it counts tens
the spot on the right in a two-digit number; it counts ones

look.title: Tens and Ones
look.cite: each number written as its tens and ones
look.prompt: What is 2 tens and 4 ones? Which row has zero ones?

check.q: In the number 58, what does the 5 mean?
check.why: The 5 is on the left, in the tens place. It means 5 tens, or 50.

check.q: What number is 3 tens and 9 ones?
check.why: 3 tens is 30. 30 and 9 is 39. Tens go first, so it is 39, not 93.

check.q: What number is 6 tens and 0 ones?
check.why: 6 tens is 60. Zero ones adds nothing. The number is 60.

lessons.title: Base-Ten Blocks
lessons.mainIdea: A long rod is one ten. A small cube is one one. Rods and cubes show any number.
reading: Math blocks called *base-ten blocks* help us count. A small cube is one. A long *rod* is ten. The rod is ten cubes stuck in a row. Count rods by tens. Count cubes by ones.
Show 45 with blocks. Take 4 rods. That is 40. Take 5 cubes. Count on: 41, 42, 43, 44, 45. Four rods and five cubes show 45.
Now show 45 another way. Use 3 rods and 15 cubes. 30 and 15 is 45. Same number. You can trade ten cubes for one rod.

words.d: blocks for counting; a cube is one and a rod is ten
a long block worth ten; the same as ten cubes

look.title: Rods and Cubes on the Mat
look.text: Look at a place-value mat. On the left side sit 5 rods. On the right side sit 2 cubes. Count the rods by tens. Ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty. Now count on the cubes. Fifty-one, fifty-two.
look.prompt: What number do the blocks show? What would you have if you added one more rod?

check.q: 2 rods and 7 cubes show what number?
check.why: 2 rods are 20. Count on 7 cubes: 21 to 27. The number is 27.

check.q: How many cubes equal one rod?
check.why: A rod is ten cubes in a row. Ten cubes equal one rod.

check.q: What number do 8 rods and 0 cubes show?
check.why: Count 8 rods by tens: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80. No cubes, so it is 80.

lessons.title: Comparing with Symbols
lessons.mainIdea: Compare tens first. If tens are the same, compare ones. Use >, < or =.
reading: Which is bigger, 52 or 38? Look at the tens. 5 tens beats 3 tens. So 52 is *greater than* 38. Write 52 > 38. The open side faces the bigger number.
Now 43 and 47. The tens are the same. Four and four. Look at the ones. 3 is less than 7. So 43 is *less than* 47. Write 43 < 47.
If both digits match, the numbers are *equal*. 29 = 29. A common mistake is to look at ones first. 19 has a 9, but 21 is bigger. Tens come first.

words.d: bigger than; the sign is >
smaller than; the sign is <
the same amount; the sign is =

look.title: The Sign Points
look.text: Think of the sign as a hungry mouth. It opens toward the bigger number. 8 > 3. The mouth opens to the 8. 3 < 8. The mouth still opens to the 8. Now try 61 and 59. Which number is bigger? Which way should the mouth open?
look.prompt: Write the sign between 61 and 59. Then write the sign between 34 and 34.

check.q: Which sign goes between 46 and 64?
check.why: 4 tens is less than 6 tens. So 46 < 64.

check.q: Which number is greater, 19 or 21?
check.why: Look at tens first. 2 tens beats 1 ten. So 21 > 19.

check.q: Which one is true?
check.why: 88 and 88 have the same digits, so they are equal. 35 is less than 53, and 72 is greater than 27.

lessons.title: Ten More and Ten Less
lessons.mainIdea: Ten more changes the tens digit up by one. Ten less changes it down by one.
reading: Nia has 34 stickers. She gets 10 more. Add one rod. 3 tens become 4 tens. The ones stay at 4. So 34 and 10 more is 44. Only the tens digit changed.
Now she gives away 10. Take away one rod. 4 tens become 3 tens. 44 take away 10 is 34. That is *ten less*. The tens digit goes down by one.
You do not need to count by ones. Find *ten more* than 57. It is 67. Ten less than 57 is 47. A common mistake is to change the ones digit. The ones stay the same.

words.d: the number you get by adding 10; the tens digit goes up by one
the number you get by taking away 10; the tens digit goes down by one

look.title: Ten More Each Time
look.cite: example: adding 10 to 23 again and again
look.prompt: What comes next after 53? What is ten less than 23?

check.q: What is 10 more than 42?
check.why: 4 tens become 5 tens. The ones stay 2. So it is 52.

check.q: What is 10 less than 78?
check.why: 7 tens become 6 tens. The ones stay 8. So it is 68.

check.q: In the table, what comes after 53?
check.why: Each row adds ten. 53 and 10 more is 63.

lessons.title: The Hundred Chart
lessons.mainIdea: On a hundred chart, each step right adds one. Each step down adds ten.
reading: A *hundred chart* shows 1 to 100. It has ten rows. Each row has ten numbers. The first row is 1 to 10. The second row is 11 to 20. The last row ends at 100.
Find 25. Move one box right. You see 26. That is one more. Move one box down. You see 35. That is ten more. Move up instead. You see 15. Ten less.
Look at a *column*. 4, 14, 24, 34, 44. The ones digit stays 4. The tens digit goes up by one. The chart shows the pattern.

words.d: a grid of numbers from 1 to 100 in ten rows of ten
a line of boxes going up and down on a chart

look.title: A Trip on the Chart
look.text: Put your finger on 41 on a hundred chart. Move down one box. Now you are on 51. Move down again. Now 61. Move one box to the right. Now 62. Move up one box. Where are you now?
look.prompt: What number is one box below 62? What number is one box to the left of 41?

check.q: On a hundred chart, what is one box below 27?
check.why: One box down is ten more. 27 and 10 more is 37.

check.q: What number comes right after 49 on the chart?
check.why: One more than 49 is 50. It starts the next row.

check.q: Which numbers are in the same column as 6?
check.why: Going down a column adds ten each time: 6, 16, 26. The ones digit stays 6.

review.q: 15 is one ten and how many ones?
review.why: 15 is ten and 5 more. So it has 5 ones.

review.q: What number is 7 tens and 2 ones?

review.why: 8 tens is more than 1 ten. So 81 > 18.
6 tens become 7 tens. The ones stay 6. So it is 76.

review.q: On a hundred chart, what is one box below 90?
review.why: One box down is ten more. 90 and 10 is 100.
24 is 2 tens and 4 ones. That is 2 rods and 4 cubes.
